newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk Ceylan plans joint plant with Japan-US firms.
newsitem.headline: Turk Ceylan plans joint plant with Japan-US firms.

text.p: Turkish Ceylan Holding plans to set up a joint integrated textile plant in northern Turkey with Japan's Mitsubishi Corp and U.S. Caynemant, part of the New York based Chantex group, a senior firm official said.

"A preliminary know-how agreement has been made with Mitsubishi and Caynemant. The Ceylan group has bought 300 hectares of land for the plant and is waiting for expropriation of some more land to be able to buy it from the state Land Office," Ali Celen, Ceylan Holding vice-chairman, told Reuters.

He said the plant to be established at Caycuma in the Black Sea province of Zonguldak would take up an area of 1,800 hectares in total and production was planned to start in two years at an initial investment cost of $200 million.
Celen said procedures for the purchase of the whole spot would take three to four months after which the project would go ahead.
He said Ceylan Holding planned to become partners with Mitsubishi and Caynemant in the integrated plant estimated to cost $1 billion when all of the production stages are completed in five years.
The integrated process will include the production phases of acrylic and viscose, thread, fabric, fabric treatment and finally readywear.
"If the integrated plant is brought to life, employment for 7,500 people will be created. Furthermore, 40 percent of production will be directed towards export," he said.
